points.summary: Peltola pledges to fight rising costs in Alaska through tax cuts, an expanded child tax credit ($3,600 per child under 6), banning price gouging, blocking anti-competitive grocery mergers, and increasing supply chain transparency to lower prices for Alaskans.
points.quote: Alaskans are being crushed by skyrocketing costs – but I will stand up to anyone to put Alaska first and fight for lower costs.

points.summary: Peltola supports 12-year congressional term limits, banning members of Congress from stock trading, requiring blind trusts for personal assets, overturning Citizens United via constitutional amendment, and passing the DISCLOSE Act for campaign finance transparency.
points.quote: Mary will fight for 12 year term limits in Congress, giving our representatives deadlines to deliver for Alaska.

points.summary: Peltola will fight to ban factory trawling in Alaska waters, keep mid-water trawlers off the ocean floor, fully fund fish stock assessments, enforce bycatch standards under the Magnuson-Stevens Act, and create Tribal seats on the North Pacific Fisheries Management Council.
points.quote: Mary will fight to ban factory trawling to protect our Alaska way of life.

points.summary: Peltola supports expanding oil and gas development including the Alaska LNG Pipeline, streamlining federal permitting, restoring renewable energy tax credits, investing in small modular nuclear reactors, geothermal, and modernizing aging energy grids across the state.
points.quote: Mary will fight every day at the federal level for projects like the Alaska LNG Pipeline, to ensure that Alaska’s energy resources are used to lower costs for Alaskans.

points.summary: Peltola will restore and expand VA healthcare, fight veteran suicide, end veteran homelessness, provide a $2,000 monthly transition stipend for up to two years, support the Major Richard Star Act, and protect the Overseas Cost of Living Allowance for military families.
points.quote: Mary will fight for a monthly transition stipend up to $2,000 for recently separated veterans for up to two years following their service

points.summary: Peltola will crack down on out-of-state corporations and hedge funds buying homes, push refundable tax credits for renters spending over 30% of income on rent, expand Indian Housing Block Grants, and tax non-resident foreign purchases of residential real estate.
points.quote: Mary will crack down on the out-of-state corporations and hedge funds buying up homes and turning neighborhoods into investment portfolios

points.summary: Peltola will eliminate federal income tax entirely for Alaskans earning under $92,000, paid by raising taxes on millionaires and billionaires, and eliminate taxes on Social Security benefits for Alaska's nearly 95,000 seniors.
points.quote: Mary will fight to cut taxes for more than half of hardworking Alaskans and eliminate federal income tax entirely for working and middle-class Alaskans earning less than $92,000 per year

points.summary: Peltola will restore funding for Bypass Mail to lower rural shipping costs, create an Essential Freight Service to reduce shipping rates statewide, and pass right-to-repair laws requiring manufacturers to provide affordable access to parts and repair instructions.
points.quote: Mary will fight to invest in and restore funding for Bypass Mail to lower shipping costs for rural Alaska and work to create an Essential Freight Service

points.summary: Opposes broad tariffs that raise consumer prices; supports antitrust enforcement, breaking up monopolies, and structural remedies; advocates lower taxes on labor, gradual minimum-wage increases, and more housing supply to reduce costs for working families.

points.summary: Seeks universal coverage by cutting total healthcare costs roughly in half through a public-private partnership combining private delivery with universal access, price discipline, and catastrophic cost protection; supports Medicaid work requirements and rural hub-and-spoke care models.

points.summary: Supports effective border security, faster asylum decisions, workplace verification, and prompt removal of security risks; advocates humane treatment of families, due process, functional legal immigration pathways, and holding employers accountable for hiring undocumented workers.

points.quote: I support ending civil asset forfeiture when no one has been convicted of a crime.

points.summary: Views education as primarily a state, local, and family responsibility; opposes federal curriculum mandates; supports federal focus on apprenticeships, technical education, industry credentials, and reducing occupational-licensing barriers; requires transparency on college outcomes before borrowing.
points.quote: Education is primarily a state, local, and family responsibility. Washington should not impose a national culture war or a one-size-fits-all curriculum.

points.summary: Chew pledges to introduce comprehensive debt reduction legislation in his first year, combining spending restraint, entitlement reform, tax base broadening, and dedicated debt-reduction revenues. He also supports honest budgeting requiring 10/20/30-year cost analysis and building a bipartisan fiscal coalition.
points.quote:
Our national debt is growing faster than our economy, and interest on that debt is consuming more of the
federal budget every year.

points.summary: Chew argues Social Security and Medicare face bankruptcy within years and demands reform within six years. He lists over a dozen specific proposals including raising retirement age, increasing payroll tax, reducing high-earner benefits, and taxing Social Security benefits, emphasizing no pain-free solution exists.
points.quote: Social Security and Medicare are going bankrupt in the next few years.

points.summary: Chew acknowledges no magic solution exists and criticizes politicians who claim otherwise. He calls for a practical, honest conversation about delivering better care at lower cost while preserving innovation and quality, drawing on his 35 years managing health insurance across multiple countries.
points.quote:
We need a practical, honest conversation about how to deliver better care at lower
cost while preserving the innovation and quality that Americans depend on.

points.summary: Chew advocates removing violent criminals and cartel traffickers while opposing use of limited government resources to pursue peaceful immigrants who contribute to the economy. He frames it as a common-sense distinction: deporting a drug kingpin makes communities safer; deporting a farm hand makes them poorer.
points.quote:
Most people agree that we should remove violent criminals and cartel traffickers from the streets to keep our communities
safe.

points.summary: Chew supports school choice empowering families to select schools meeting their children's needs with financial support. He opposes politicized ideological agendas in schools, advocates local control over federal bureaucratic dictates, and emphasizes teaching critical thinking and workforce-relevant skills.
points.quote:
Parents deserve real choices. We should empower families to choose the schools that best meet
their children’s needs and provide support so they can afford it.

points.summary: Chew supports an all-of-above energy strategy with heavy reliance on nuclear power, citing his nuclear submarine service. He specifically advocates investing in small modular reactors and argues wind and solar alone cannot meet energy demands from data centers, cloud computing, and AI.
points.quote: I support an all-of-above energy strategy that includes a heavy reliance on nuclear power.

points.summary: Chew supports Ukraine against Russia, countering China's military ambitions, maintaining Middle East stability, and watching North Korea and Iran. He criticizes Trump's unilateral Iran war as reckless, arguing it emboldened Iranian extremists and collapsed American strategic influence.
points.quote:
We must support Ukraine against Russian aggression, counter China’s growing military ambitions, maintain stability in the Middle East, and watch out for threats from North
Korea and Iran.

points.summary: Chew frames Colorado's housing crisis as supply-and-demand, exacerbated by high mortgage rates linked to national debt, tariffs, immigration restrictions, and overbearing environmental regulations. His solution: tame deficits, reduce tariffs, welcome immigration labor, and repeal costly regulations.
points.quote: If we want to build more affordable housing, we need to tame our national deficits, reduce tariffs, welcome immigration labor, and repeal costly regulations.

points.summary: Tennessee is short roughly 120,000 starter homes. points.quote: The state helps pay for the water, sewer, and road work a city would otherwise push onto the developer.

points.summary: Hatley would create an elected, nonpartisan State Auditor with CPA credentials, forensic-audit and subpoena authority, and whistleblower protections. He would also rebuild the state spending portal so every contract, grant, and payment is posted within 30 days in plain English, and ban campaign contributions from significant state contractors while they seek or perform state work.
points.quote: an independent, nonpartisan State Auditor — elected statewide, just like 24 other states

points.summary: Hatley pledges to be the toughest governor on crime, focusing on clearing the crime-lab backlog, hiring detectives and forensic scientists, expanding TBI's violent-crime team, and giving rural sheriffs regional investigators. He would also make life without parole mandatory for repeat child sex offenders and cut recidivism in half through pre-release reentry planning.
points.quote: David Hatley will be the toughest governor this state has seen on crime

points.summary: Hatley would impose a moratorium on new data-center approvals until Tennessee enacts real rules, ending PILOTs and tax abatements. At least half of new tax revenue from data centers would go to cutting property taxes for homeowners in the hosting county, and companies would pay for their own power and water capacity.
points.quote: David Hatley would pause new approvals until Tennessee writes real rules, and ends the giveaways: no PILOTs, no abatements.

points.summary: Hatley would ban or restrict the use of Flock facial-recognition cameras, arguing the system is flawed, invasive, and leads to wrongful stops of innocent citizens. He states he will be tough on crime but believes the current surveillance system violates the privacy of average Tennesseans.
points.quote: Flock cameras are getting abused far too often across our great state.

points.summary: Hatley aims to move Tennessee into the top ten nationally in reading within four years (NAEP-measured). points.quote: David Hatley’s goal is top ten in reading in the nation within four years

points.summary: On drugs, Hatley would triple TBI's drug division to about 150 agents, create Florida-style SAFE grants for local task forces targeting large traffickers, add a financial-crimes unit, require medication-assisted treatment in every county jail, and publish one public accounting of opioid settlement money.

points.summary: Hatley would eliminate Tennessee's 4% state sales tax on groceries, returning roughly $400 per year to the average family. points.quote: I will eliminate the state sales tax on groceries.
